This refers to kigurumi where the facial features are modeled primarily after anime characters. On the internet, they are referred to as "Bishojo Kigurumi" (beautiful girl kigurumi). Basically, the eyes and mouth are deformed to be larger and the nose is made smaller; they are not realistic. This deformation is an exaggerated expression derived from psychological sensations (such as "cute" or "beautiful"). They are often designed with "moe" in mind.

The head of such a kigurumi is created using an FRP (Fiber-reinforced plastic) base, upon which a wig is placed. The final shape is achieved by applying flesh-colored paint and attaching eyes made from materials such as plastic sheets, smoked glass, or waterproof paper.

According to community surveys, it is estimated that approximately 90% of enthusiasts who enjoy wearing these types of kigurumi are male.

This type of kigurumi includes both cosplay versions based on characters from manga and anime, as well as original characters created through the imagination of the kigurumi maker.
